A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE coactivation study. All 29 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison; figures and tables were matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original ablation, steering, component-organization, and baseline-comparison results, with additional Gemma 2 9B, taxonomy, and transcoder experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports steering-strength sensitivity results and categorized steering failures.

M1.justification: The top-5 feature selection, correlation-threshold graph construction, density pruning, component selection, and ablation/amplification procedure remain. V3 clarifies intervention implementation and discusses future automated selection; neither establishes a new implemented method. Omitting edge-weight notation leaves the connectivity-based component procedure unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 10 countries, 11 translated words and three target languages, eight verbs and five transformations, and supplementary taxonomy coverage. Changing the introductory task count from four to three corrects the enumeration. Expanded acceptable-answer lists concern scoring.

E2.justification: Section 3.4 retains the same most-causally-impactful single-feature baseline, reporting country-task success rates of 83%, 83%, and 75%. Newly cited steering methods are discussed but are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix G revises selected relation-steering strengths from 0.45 for all three tasks to 0.40, 0.40, and 0.65, and revises several composite strengths. Appendix B changes accepted answers, while Appendix G adds relation-specific tuning. These are reported setting changes within retained evaluations; newly disclosed generation and matching rules do not establish that those procedures changed.

E4.justification: V3 newly reports complete steering-strength sensitivity tables and a separate relation-specific tuning analysis in Appendix G. New Appendix J and Figure 13 systematically classify failures across all three tasks and steering types, substantially extending v2's selected-setting results and scattered failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sensitivity results and failure counts do not introduce uncertainty estimation; task averages and regression lines remain point summaries.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises translation relation-steering success from 0.92 to 0.98 and composite success from 0.92/0.59/0.22 to 0.90/0.64/0.19 for country facts/translation/verb transformations. Table 5 and numerous appendix entries also change, while Tables 9-11 and Figure 13 add sensitivity and failure results. Revised strengths and answer keys prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2 explicitly defines edge weights as w(e) = min(1.0, rho); v3 omits this definition. The remaining feature-selection, thresholding, and component definitions are retained, with no new theorems, proofs, or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: V3 softens the abstract's final mechanistic inference by dropping the assertion that modular knowledge is accessed through compositional operations, while retaining composable-steering claims. The introduction now explicitly foregrounds up to 98% individual and 90% composite steering success. The central causal-module and hierarchical-organization contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 expands failure interpretation substantially: residual aquatic knowledge may explain fish-related translation outputs, capitalization components may encode output style, and prompted relations may remain distributed beyond ablated components. It also distinguishes automated extraction from manual component selection and discusses potential automation. These extend v2's shorter explanations and limitations.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-availability link and specifies SAE decoding after interventions and amplification relative to observed maximum activations. Appendix B newly explains the five-token generation limit, answer matching, word-boundary exceptions, and case handling; Appendix G updates selected hyperparameters. These substantially improve documentation of previously unspecified reproduction details.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion of Bayat et al. and Dumas et al. on steering and composability, plus citations to DiCarlo, LeCun, and Mikolov. It removes the Xie et al. neuronal-population analogy. This is a focused positioning expansion; publication-metadata updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: V3 restructures the introduction into explicit findings, clarifies method and task descriptions, edits experimental discussion, and renames Section 3.5 from Cross-Task Evaluation to Specificity Evaluation. It adds acknowledgments and Appendix J, while retaining the main section sequence and much existing exposition.

P2.justification: V3 adds three sensitivity tables and the nine-panel failure Figure 13, redraws the pipeline figure, and reorganizes Figure 4 with clearer axes. Main token tables expand from three displayed tokens to five, partly redisplaying existing appendix material. Table headings and appendix layouts are also revised; most earlier component figures remain.

improvement.justification: Explicit intervention and scoring details, a code pointer, and sensitivity and failure analyses make v3 easier to reproduce and assess. The gain is limited by unresolved reporting inconsistencies: new Figure 13 reports 24 country concept-steering failures, whereas Table 20's trial counts and success rates imply 12. The clearer documentation nevertheless provides a modest net improvement to the retained study.
